notes: Two panel pages were loading a file that was never included in the download, so a piece of each quietly did nothing. The Panel Editor's Spacing tab and the original Gauge theme both ask the same component which shape a panel is — landscape, portrait, square, ultrawide or tall — and that component was missing from every release so far. Both fell back to guessing landscape instead of saying anything was wrong. It is now included.

The build now refuses to ship a page that loads a file the download does not contain. The existing check only followed the app's own code and could not see a page's scripts and stylesheets, which is how the above went unnoticed through every release.

Filling in the panel capability sheet now changes the app directly. Until now the sheet wrote its answers to a file nothing read, and someone had to copy them into the code by hand for anything to happen. The app reads that file itself now, so ticking a setting on and off is the change. A panel with nothing filled in yet behaves exactly as it does today.
The lowest-tier dropdown on that sheet now does something. It used to record a choice nothing acted on; a setting set above your plan is shown locked rather than simply appearing.
Corner radius was a working panel setting that was missing from the capability sheet entirely. It is on the list now, so it cannot be dropped by accident.

The Control Panel has a new look. Obsidian Glint is Sigil's own design system — true black, a single rustic gold, and the instrument-panel density of the hardware panel. It is the default now, on every plan including the free one, so it is simply what the app looks like.
The previous look, Obsidian Gold, has been retired from the theme picker. If you were on it you will be moved to the new default automatically; nothing needs doing.

NovaPanel is now Sigil everywhere in the Control Panel — the titlebar, Settings, the Panel Editor and the first-run scan. The old NovaPanel mark has been removed until Sigil's own is ready, so the wordmark now stands on its own, set in the brand face.
The plan ladder gained an owner-only level above the rest, for internal tools that are never sold and never appear on a pricing page.

Developer surfaces — the Debug and Testing tabs and Installed Modules — now ask for that owner level by name rather than for whatever happens to sit at the top of the ladder. That is what stops them drifting into a paying customer's reach the day the plan names change. Installs already at the old top are moved up once, automatically, so nothing you could reach before goes missing.
